title: Whether the Lazarus story already happened or images the coming judgment
english: Have these things already happened, and has each person been allotted the recompense he deserved? Or does he prefigure in them the coming judgment? But, the objector says, since Christ names the name of Lazarus, it truly happened and was enacted. For why did Jesus not say, “Some poor man,” but “Lazarus”? So that by the name he might show that these things actually happened. Solution: the judgment, etc. Question 9.
translator_notes: True OET from PG 77 / Vat. gr. 447 Greek; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify; skip Pusey-PD / Greystone / Lunn / Hill.
orientation: An unnamed interlocutor raises the question whether the rich man and Lazarus account has already been enacted with due recompense, or whether it images the coming judgment, and argues from the naming of Lazarus that it truly happened.

title: Two further questions: Hosea's marriage and Melchizedek's origin
english: Did the prophet Hosea take a prostitute as his wife and beget children by her in deed and actuality? Or does he say these things understood prophetically? Or again: Is Melchizedek not simply a man, nor a spirit, but a man having no origin of his coming into being from humans, newly created by God?
translator_notes: True OET from PG 77 / Vat. gr. 447 Greek; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify; skip Pusey-PD / Greystone / Lunn / Hill.
orientation: After the interlocutor's argument about Lazarus, the fragment poses two further questions for solution: whether Hosea really married a prostitute and had children by her in actual deed, and what kind of being Melchizedek was.

title: Where to find fuller discussion of these questions
english: I have already written at length about these questions in my commentary on the prophet Hosea, and in my work On Genesis you will find a thorough examination of Melchizedek. Your reverence can read those books and learn from them the meaning of what has been said on each point.
